I have a slight preference for deep, focused conversations on a single topic, though I don't mind jumping between subjects now and then.

What I like about focused conversations is that they let us go beyond surface-level takes. When we stick with one topic, we can unpack nuances, challenge each other's assumptions, and actually build on what the other person is saying instead of just skimming through ideas. It feels more meaningful to me when I can sense that we're both really engaging with the topic rather than just checking boxes of small talk.

That said, some of my favorite conversations have been the ones where we start with one thing and naturally meander into three or four other related topics—like going from talking about a specific book, to the author's life, to how that book changed your perspective on something, to a completely different book that made you feel the same way. That organic flow feels different from forced topic-hopping, and I enjoy that too.
